principles: the currently serving release is never a recovery candidate
during candidate soak or hold, the preserved canonical release is recovery rank 1
after admission, prior distinct qualified canonical releases form the recovery ladder newest-first
a candidate is source-ready only when a fresh repo-local OIDC source proof still covers that exact commit
the safest recovery candidate is the lowest-numbered rank with fresh sourceAvailable proof
history-building targets with no prior qualified canonical release are not failures
Railway-native image retention is not inferred from Git source availability
Defence recommends recovery candidates but never performs rollback automatically
